allies.rationale_text: Systems-thinking complements gestalt-principles-of-perception by helping a visible whole map onto real interrelationships instead of isolated parts.
allies.source_quote: Systems thinking focuses on interrelationships and feedback loops. Gestalt provides a way of perceiving the whole before the parts.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical describes Gestalt as 'integral to the concept of a latticework of theory' — systems thinking focuses on seeing interrelationships, patterns, and wholes, sharing the core principle of perceiving organized totalities.
allies.activation_condition: When understanding a complex situation requires perceiving organized patterns and interrelationships rather than analyzing individual components in isolation

allies.rationale_text: Cognitive-load-theory strengthens gestalt-principles-of-perception by turning structured grouping into lower cognitive burden and faster comprehension.
allies.source_quote: By promoting the organization of information into structured chunks or schemas, Gestalt reduces cognitive load.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical states Gestalt 'reduces cognitive load' by 'promoting the organization of information into structured chunks or schemas', supporting perceptual organization for efficient processing.
allies.activation_condition: When information must be organized into perceptual schemas to reduce the working memory burden of processing unstructured individual data points

antagonists.rationale_text: Einstellung-effect undermines gestalt-principles-of-perception by locking the brain onto the first recognized pattern, preventing the reorganization of sensory data into a more accurate or useful whole.
antagonists.source_quote: The most significant danger is that the brain's preference for recognized patterns (Gestalts) leads to cognitive biases. This is often called the law of the instrument or Maslow's hammer.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Pattern fixation can lock perception into familiar gestalt interpretations, preventing recognition of genuinely novel patterns that don't fit established perceptual frameworks.
antagonists.activation_condition: When familiar perceptual patterns dominate interpretation, causing novel configurations to be force-fitted into known gestalts rather than perceived on their own terms

antagonists.rationale_text: Theory-induced-blindness undermines gestalt-principles-of-perception by making the brain resist evidence that challenges an established perceptual organization, treating a satisfying pattern as settled truth rather than a provisional frame.
antagonists.source_quote: Once a coherent pattern (model) is established, the brain resists evidence that challenges it, leading to model-defending behavior. This often prevents rewriting models of reality.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Theoretical frameworks can create blind spots in perceptual grouping — related to canonical warning that 'overreliance on perceived coherence of a Gestalt can hide flaws'.
antagonists.activation_condition: When theoretical commitment to a particular gestalt interpretation creates blind spots that hide flaws in the perceived coherence

structured_tensions.tension_text: Gestalt-principles-of-perception conflicts with representativeness-heuristic when a familiar-looking pattern is treated as evidence of the underlying cause.
structured_tensions.source_quote: gestalt-principles-of-perception conflicts with representativeness-heuristic (representativeness heuristic) when surface pattern grouping is treated as causal proof.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Gestalt-principles-of-perception conflicts with confirmation-bias when observers select the arrangement that supports what they already believe.
structured_tensions.source_quote: gestalt-principles-of-perception conflicts with confirmation-bias (confirmation bias) when observers privilege perceptual arrangements that support prior beliefs.
